newsitem.title: UK: "Pocket Budget" summary issued by UK Treasury 2.
newsitem.headline: "Pocket Budget" summary issued by UK Treasury 2.

text.p: "Pocket budget" summary part two --
ENCOURAGING LONG-TERM INVESTMENT
The key to future success is investment in infrastructure, technology and people.
To help promote investment, the Budget:
cuts corporation tax rates from 1 April 1997;
makes other tax changes to encourage companies to invest profits in the future;
re-invests money from council house sales in housing.
MODERNISING THE WELFARE STATE
The present welfare state has to be modernised to stop people being trapped in poverty without the skills they need to get jobs.

The Budget announces a 5.2 billion Welfare to Work package, paid for by the windfall tax on the excess profits of the privatised utilities, to give people the skills and opportunities to play a full role in society:
a New Deal for the young and long-term unemployed;
a New Deal to help lone parents find work and childcare as part of the Government's national childcare strategy;
a New Deal for schools with an extra 1.3 billion to improve school buildings and equipment.
THE NEW DEAL FOR THE YOUNG AND LONG-TERM UNEMPLOYED
The Budget introduces a 3.5 billion sterling New Deal
package to attack unemployment and reduce spending on social security.
There are four options for 18-25 year-olds unemployed for
six months or more:
-- a job attracting a wage subsidy of 60 sterling per
week (paid to employers for six months);
-- a six month work placement with an Environmental Task
Force on which participants will be paid a trainee wage of 15 more than benefits;
-- a work placement with a voluntary organisation on which participants will also be paid a trainee wage of 15 more than benefits;
-- a place on a full-time education and training course during which they will continue to receive full benefit.
For anyone who has been unemployed for two years, employers will be offered a subsidy of 75 (sterling) a week for six months as an incentive to recruit and train them.
THE NEW DEAL FOR SCHOOLS
One of the main causes of unemployment is

under-achievement at school. Tackling this is an ssential part of the Welfare to Work package. 1.3 billion from the windfall tax will be spent on buildings and equipment to make sure school leavers have the skills to secure real and lasting jobs.
The Government also wants the tax and benefits system to encourage - not discourage - work and enterprise. A review has been set up to help achieve this.
PROVIDING HIGH QUALITY PUBLIC SERVICES
The Government spends 320 billion a year - four out of every ten pounds this country earns or over 5,000 for every man, woman and child.

The Government believes spending is not the solution to every problem - it is how money is spent that counts. The Government is committed to tight control of spending but has found extra funds for top priorities next year:
-- an extra 1 billion for local authorities to spend on education, in addition to the 1.3 billion
--. from the windfall tax;
-- an extra 1.2 billion for the National Health Service.
THE PRIVATE FINANCE INITIATIVE
The Private Finance Initiative (PFI) is simply a new way

for the Government to buy services for the public. The Government decides what service it wants to provide, then the private sector finds the best way to design, build, finance and operate that service in partnership with the public sector. The Government has already re-invigorated the PFI with a range of measures to streamline the process. The potential for greater use of public, private partnerships will be explored in the Governments review of spending.

For the longer term, the Government has announced a comprehensive spending review to ensure it makes best use of your money. Its aim is to reshape spending to support investment, employment,opportunity and fairness.
The Government sees partnership between the public and the private sector as the key to delivering high quality public services at value for money for the taxpayer.
MOVING TOWARDS A FAIRER TAX SYSTEM
We need taxes to pay for our public services. The Government believes the tax system should:
-- encourage work - making it worth people's while to work instead of staying on benefit;
-- promote savings and investment - creating the right climate and incentives for long-term investment;
-- be fair - for the benefit of the many, not the few;
-- be seen to be fair - being tough on tax avoidance and evasion;
To start to meet these aims, the Budget will:
--reduce VAT on fuel bills from 8 per cent to 5 per cent. This will come into effect on 1 September - in time for winter;
-- abolish tax relief on private medical insurance for the over-60s;
-- crack down on tax avoidance and close loopholes.
PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT AND HEALTH
The Government places high priority on protecting the environment for future generations and is prepared to use taxes to protect the environment and health.
The Budget:
-- introduces a statement of intent on the role of taxes in environmental policy;
-- increases duty on petrol and diesel immediately;
-- increases tax on tobacco from December;
-- increases vehicle excise duties for licences taken out after 15 November. Reductions for "clean" buses and lorries will follow;
-- announces a study on the environmental costs of quarrying and consultation on options to reduce water pollution.
